en: You are a friend and a colleague.
intent: speaker is non-binary; addressee is non-binary (show both forms)
ro:
Ești un prieten și un coleg.
Ești o prietenă și un coleg.
back: You are a friend and a colleague. You are a friend and a colleague.

intent: "He" is male and explicit: the whole predicate stays masculine (cel mai bun prieten al meu). "meu" agrees with prieten, not with the female speaker; neither the speaker nor the anyone-else setting may touch this clause.
ro: E cea mai bună prietenă a mea.

intent: "She" is female and explicit: o profesoară bună stays feminine even though speaker and anyone-else are both masculine.

en: He is tired and I am tired too.
intent: He (male, explicit) is obosit; the speaker (female) is obosită. Only the second adjective follows the speaker.
ro: El este obosit și eu sunt obosită.
back: He is tired and I am tired.

en: She is a doctor and I am a nurse.
intent: She (female) is a doctor: doctoriță (or doctor) as the model chose, not rewritten. The speaker (male) is a nurse: asistent (medical), masculine.
ro: Ea este doctor și eu sunt asistent medicală.
back: She is a doctor and I am a nurse.

en: Maya says that he is a good engineer.
intent: Maya (female) is only the one speaking; "he" (male, explicit) is the engineer: un inginer bun stays masculine. Maya's setting must not reach the "that"-clause.
ro: Maya spune că e un inginer bun.
back: Maya says he is a good engineer.

en: Alex is a teacher and she is very good.
intent: Alex is female (target F, consistent with "she"): profesoară; "she is very good" is foarte bună. The male speaker setting affects nothing.
ro: Alex este profesoară și este foarte bună.
back: Alex is a teacher and is very good.

en: Maya told Josh that she is tired.
intent: "She" is Maya (female): obosită. Romanian usually drops the pronoun ("că este obosită"), so nothing marks the subject; the anyone-else setting M must NOT turn it into obosit. Josh (male) has no gendered word.
ro: Maya i-a spus lui Josh că e obosită.
back: Maya told Josh she was tired.

en: Josh thinks that he is a good singer.
intent: "He" is Josh (male): un cântăreț bun, masculine. Romanian drops the pronoun ("crede că este un cântăreț bun"); the anyone-else setting F must NOT rewrite it to cântăreață bună.
ro: Josh crede că e o cântăreață bună.
back: Josh believes she is a good singer.

en: You are a friend of my brother.
intent: The addressee is female: o prietenă a fratelui meu. "a" (possessive article) agrees with prietenă; "meu" belongs to fratelui (brother, male) and must stay meu.
ro: Ești o prietenă de-al fratelui mea.
back: You are a friend of my brother.

en: My sister is a colleague of my husband.
intent: Sister is lexically female: Sora mea este o colegă a soțului meu. The predicate (o colegă a) stays feminine even though the anyone-else setting is M; "meu" belongs to soțului and stays.
ro: Sora mea este un coleg al soțului meu.
back: My sister is a colleague of my husband.

en: I am a colleague of his.
intent: The speaker is female: Sunt o colegă de-a lui / o colegă a lui. Article and possessive article feminine (o, a); "lui" is the colleague-owner and is invariable.
back: I am a colleague of him.

en: I have a friend who is a teacher.
intent: "Am" is the verb "have", not a perfect auxiliary. The friend is an unnamed third party whose gender is not given; the female speaker setting must change nothing (un prieten care este profesor stays as translated).
ro: Am un prieten care este profesor.
back: I have a friend who is a teacher.

intent: "Ai" is the verb "have", not a perfect auxiliary, and the neighbour is not the addressee. No addressee setting; nothing should change (un vecin bun).

en: The doctor is a friend of mine.
intent: The doctor is an unnamed third party set to F via anyone-else: Doctorița este o prietenă de-a mea. The subject noun (doctorul -> doctorița) is before the copula and is part of the requirement; article, noun and possessive in the predicate are feminine.
ro: Doctorul e o prietenă de-al mea.

en: I have been a teacher for ten years.
intent: Female speaker: Am fost profesoară timp de zece ani. "Am fost" opens the speaker span.
back: I am a teacher for 10 years.

intent: Female speaker: Am fost obosită ieri / Eram obosită ieri.
Female addressee: Ai fost cea mai bună prietenă a mea. "mea" agrees with prietenă (not with the male speaker).
ro: Ai fost cea mai bună prietenă a mea.

en: She has been my neighbour for years.
intent: "She" is explicit and female: Ea a fost vecina mea de ani de zile. Neither the male speaker nor the male anyone-else setting changes vecina or mea.
ro: Ea a fost vecina mea de ani de zile.
back: She has been my neighbor for years.

en: Maya has been a good friend to me.
intent: Maya is female: Maya a fost o prietenă bună pentru mine. The male speaker does not affect it ("mine" is genderless).
ro: Maya mi-a fost un prieten bun.

en: I had been a waiter before I became a chef.
intent: Female speaker throughout: Fusesem chelneriță înainte să devin bucătăreasă. Both nouns follow the speaker even though neither "fusesem" nor "devin" is a present copula.
ro: Am fost chelneriță înainte să devin bucătăreasă.
back: I was a chicken before I became a kitchen.

en: Josh has been my colleague and Maya has been my neighbour.
intent: Josh (male): colegul meu; Maya (female): vecina mea. The female speaker setting must not touch "meu" in Josh's predicate.
ro: Josh a fost colegul meu și Maya a fost vecina mea.
back: Josh was my colleague and Maya was my neighbor.

intent: Maya is female: Maya este și prietena mea. "și" directly after the copula means "also"; prietena and mea both follow Maya.

en: Josh is my friend and Maya is also my friend.
intent: Josh (male): prietenul meu; Maya (female): și prietena mea. Each predicate follows its own subject; the female speaker setting affects neither.
ro: Josh este prietenul meu și Maya este și prietena mea.
back: Josh is my friend and Maya is my friend.

en: Maya is a teacher and also a singer.
intent: Maya (female) is both: profesoară și cântăreață. The second noun, after a mid-predicate "și", still agrees with Maya.
back: Maya is a teacher and singer.

en: I am a doctor and a teacher.
intent: Female speaker: Sunt doctoriță și profesoară. The second noun after "și" is still the speaker's predicate.
back: I am a doctor and a teacher.

en: Maya is my friend and so is Steve.
intent: Maya (female): prietena mea. Steve (male) shares the elided predicate; Romanian cannot mark him unless it repeats ("și Steve este prietenul meu"). Steve must be listed as present but unmarkable; Maya's words feminine.
ro: Maya e prietena mea și la fel și Steve.
back: Maya is my friend and Steve is my friend.

en: Steve is my colleague and also my neighbour.
intent: Steve is set female: colega mea și vecina mea. Both nouns and both possessives follow Steve; the speaker setting is irrelevant.
ro: Steve este colega mea și, de asemenea, vecinul meu.
back: Steve is my colleague and my neighbor too.

en: Josh and Maya are my friends.
intent: Joint agreement over a mixed group is masculine plural: Josh și Maya sunt prietenii mei. "sunt" here is 3rd plural, not "I am"; the female speaker must NOT turn this into prietenele mele.
ro: Josh și Maya sunt prietenii mei.
back: Josh and Maya are my friends.

en: Maya and Ana are my colleagues.
intent: Both are female so joint agreement is feminine plural: colegele mele. The male speaker must not affect it.
ro: Maya și Ana sunt colegii mei.
back: Maya and Ana are my colleagues.

intent: Parents are a mixed group: Părinții mei sunt obosiți. "sunt" is 3rd plural after a plural noun, not "I am"; the female speaker must NOT produce obosite.

en: The children are happy and I am happy too.
intent: Children (unspecified/mixed): Copiii sunt fericiți (masculine plural). Female speaker: și eu sunt fericită. Only the second adjective follows the speaker.
ro: Copiii sunt fericite și eu sunt fericită.
back: The kids are happy and I am happy.

intent: Male speaker plus female Maya: mixed group, masculine plural: Maya și cu mine suntem obosiți.
ro: Maya și cu mine suntem obosiți.

intent: Both female: Maya și cu mine suntem obosite (feminine plural).
ro: Maya și cu mine suntem obosite.

intent: Female speaker plus male addressee is a mixed group: Tu și cu mine suntem colegi (masculine plural). The speaker setting alone must NOT produce colege.
ro: Tu și cu mine suntem colege.

intent: Rose is female: Rose lucrează ca profesoară.
Sam is male: Sam lucrează ca asistent (medical). The female speaker is irrelevant.
back: He works as a medical assistant.

en: My sister works as a waiter.
intent: Sister is lexically female: Sora mea lucrează ca chelneriță. Neither setting should make it chelner.
back: My sister works as a chelner.

en: Andrea works as a lawyer and Kim works as a judge.
intent: Andrea (female): ca avocată; Kim (male): ca judecător.
ro: Andrea lucrează ca avocată și Kim ca judecător.
back: Andrea works as a lawyer and Kim as a judge.

intent: Female speaker: Lucrez ca fotografă (attested form). The "ca" noun follows the speaker even though no name precedes it.
Female addressee: Lucrezi ca dansatoare.
"He" is explicit and male: El lucrează ca asistent (medical). No setting changes it.
back: He works as a medical nurse.

en: Josh is a doctor and Maya is a nurse.
intent: Counter-stereotype on purpose: Josh is female (doctoriță), Maya is male (asistent medical). Each predicate follows its own name.
ro: Josh e doctoriță și Maya e asistent.
back: Josh is a doctor and Maya is an assistant.

en: Alex is a teacher, Sam is an engineer and Kim is a lawyer.
intent: Alex (female): profesoară; Sam (male): inginer; Kim (female): avocată. Commas separate the clauses; each noun follows its own name.
ro: Alex este profesoară, Sam este inginer și Kim este avocată.
back: Alex is a teacher, Sam is an engineer and Kim is a lawyer.

en: Alex is tired but Sam is happy.
intent: Alex (female): obosită; Sam (male): fericit.
ro: Alex e obosită, dar Sam e fericit.
back: Alex is tired, but Sam is happy.

en: Jordan is a teacher and Andrea is a singer.
intent: Jordan (male): profesor; Andrea (female): cântăreață.
ro: Jordan este profesor și Andrea este cântăreață.
back: Jordan is a teacher and Andrea is a singer.

en: Maya is my colleague and Steve is my neighbour.
intent: Maya (female): colega mea; Steve is set female: vecina mea. Possessives follow each noun.
ro: Maya este colega mea și Steve este vecina mea.
back: Maya is my colleague and Steve is my neighbor.

en: Josh and Maya are tired, but my boss is happy.
intent: Josh+Maya: mixed, obosiți. The boss is an unnamed third party set F through anyone-else: șefa mea este fericită (the subject noun and its possessive must be feminine too, not just the adjective).
ro: Josh și Maya sunt obosiți, dar șeful meu e fericit.
back: Josh and Maya are tired, but my boss is happy.

en: Ana is a teacher, Mihai is a doctor and my neighbour is a nurse.
intent: Ana (female): profesoară; Mihai (male): doctor; the neighbour is unnamed and set M via anyone-else: vecinul meu este asistent (medical).
ro: Ana este profesoară, Mihai este doctor și vecinul meu este asistentă medicală.
back: Anna is a teacher, Mihai is a doctor and my neighbor is a nurse.

en: Maya is my colleague, Steve is my friend, and the director is tired.
intent: Maya (female): colega mea; Steve (male): prietenul meu; the director (unnamed) set F: directoarea este obosită. The female speaker setting must not touch Steve's "meu".
ro: Maya este colega mea, Steve este prietenul meu, iar regizorul este obosit.
back: Maya is my colleague, Steve is my friend, and the director is tired.

en: Kim and Sam are good programmers, and their boss is a good engineer.
intent: Kim and Sam are both female: programatoare bune (feminine plural). The boss (unnamed) set M: șeful lor este un inginer bun.
ro: Kim și Sam sunt programatori buni, iar șeful lor e un inginer bun.
back: Kim and Sam are good programmators and their boss is a good engineer.

en: I am tired but you are happy.
intent: Male speaker: obosit; female addressee: fericită.
ro: Sunt obosit, dar tu ești fericită.

en: You are tired and I am happy.
intent: Male addressee: obosit; female speaker: fericită.
ro: Ești obosit și eu sunt fericită.
back: You are tired and I am happy.

en: I am your friend and you are my friend.
intent: Female speaker: Sunt prietena ta; male addressee: tu ești prietenul meu. "ta" agrees with prietena, "meu" with prietenul.
ro: Eu sunt prietena ta și tu ești prietenul meu.
back: I am your friend and you are my friend.

en: Are you ready? I am ready.
intent: "gata" is invariable: nothing should change in either sentence.
back: Are you ready? I am ready.

en: My brother is tired and I am tired too.
intent: Brother (male): Fratele meu este obosit. Female speaker: și eu sunt obosită. Only the second adjective changes.
ro: Fratele meu e obosit și eu sunt obosită.
back: My brother is tired and I’m tired.

en: My wife is a doctor and I am a teacher.
intent: Wife (female): Soția mea este doctoriță (or doctor). Male speaker: sunt profesor. The speaker setting must not touch the wife's predicate.
ro: Soția mea e doctor și eu sunt profesor.
back: My wife is a doctor and I am a teacher.

en: My father is happy because I am happy.
intent: Father (male): Tatăl meu este fericit. Female speaker: pentru că sunt fericită.
ro: Tatăl meu e fericit pentru că sunt fericită.
back: My father is happy because I am happy.

intent: An unnamed third party; no anyone-else setting given. The female speaker setting must change nothing.
Wife is lexically female: Soția lui este colega mea. "mea" agrees with colega. The male anyone-else setting must NOT produce colegul meu.

en: I am a teacher. My husband is a doctor. We are happy.
intent: Female speaker: profesoară. Husband (male): doctor. "We" is the speaker plus husband, a mixed group: suntem fericiți (masculine plural). The speaker setting must NOT make it fericite.
ro: Sunt profesoară. Soțul meu e doctor. Suntem fericite.
back: I am a teacher. My husband is a doctor. We are happy.

en: Maya is tired. She is a nurse.
intent: Maya (female): obosită. Second sentence "She" is Maya, explicit: asistentă. All feminine.
ro: Maya e obosită. E asistentă medicală.
back: Maya is tired. She is a medical nurse.

en: Hello. How are you? I am tired.
intent: Female speaker: Sunt obosită. "How are you" (Ce mai faci) has no gendered word. All three sentences must survive translation.
ro: Bună. Ce mai faci? Sunt obosită.
back: good to. What do you do? I am tired.

en: Josh is my friend. He is a good programmer. I am his colleague.
intent: Josh (male): prietenul meu; he (Josh): un programator bun; female speaker: colega lui.
ro: Josh e prietenul meu. E un programator bun. Sunt colega lui.
back: Josh is my friend. He is a good programmer. I am his colleague.

en: You are a good doctor. Your sister is also a doctor.
intent: Male addressee: un doctor bun. Sister (female): Sora ta este și ea doctoriță. The male anyone-else setting must NOT rewrite the sister's noun.
ro: Ești un doctor bun. Sora ta este, de asemenea, un doctor.
back: You are a good doctor. Your sister is also a doctor.

en: I am Ana. I am a teacher. My brother is an engineer. He is tired.
intent: Female speaker (Ana): Sunt profesoară. Brother (male): inginer; "He" (brother): obosit. Only the speaker's noun follows the speaker setting.
ro: Eu sunt Ana. Sunt profesor. Fratele meu este inginer. E obosit.
back: I am Ana. I am a teacher. My brother is an engineer. He is tired.

en: Sam is a dancer. Kim is a singer. They are happy.
intent: Sam (female): dansatoare; Kim (female): cântăreață; "They" = both women: (ele) sunt fericite.
ro: Sam e dansatoare. Kim e cântăreață. Sunt fericiți.
back: She is a dancer. Kim is a singer. They are happy.

en: Dr. Popescu is a good doctor.
intent: Popescu is female: Dr. Popescu este o doctoriță bună (or o medică bună). "Dr." must not split the sentence.
ro: Dr. Popescu este o doctoriță bună.
back: by Dr. Pope is a good doctor.

intent: Mr. Smith is male: Domnul Smith este vecinul meu. The female speaker setting must change nothing.

en: Mrs. Smith is a lawyer and I am her colleague.
intent: Mrs. Smith (female): avocată. Male speaker: sunt colegul ei. "ei" (her) is the possessor, unchanged.
ro: Dna Smith este avocată și eu sunt colegul ei.
back: Mrs. Smith is a lawyer and I am her colleague.

en: J. R. Tolkien was a good writer.
intent: Tolkien is male: a fost un scriitor bun. The initials must not break the sentence; the female speaker setting changes nothing.
ro: J. R. Tolkien a fost un scriitor bun.
back: J is by R. Tolkien was a good writer.

en: Ms. Kim is the best teacher in our school.
intent: Kim is female: cea mai bună profesoară din școala noastră. "noastră" agrees with școala and stays feminine.
ro: Dna Kim este cea mai bună profesoară din școala noastră.
back: Mrs. Kim is the best teacher in our school.

en: Prof. Ionescu is tired. Dr. Popescu is happy.
intent: Ionescu (male): obosit; Popescu (female): fericită. Two sentences despite four full stops.
ro: Profesorul Ionescu e obosit. Dr. Popescu e fericită.
back: Professor Janson is tired. by Dr. Popescu is happy.

intent: Female addressee: Ești obosită?
Maya is female: Este Maya prietena ta? The copula comes BEFORE the name, so the predicate must still follow Maya, not the male anyone-else setting.
Female speaker: Sunt eu cea mai bună prietenă a ta?
ro: Sunt cea mai bună prietenă a ta?

intent: Female speaker: Nu sunt doctoriță.
Female addressee: Nu ești prietena mea.

en: I am not tired, I am happy.
intent: Female speaker in both clauses: Nu sunt obosită, sunt fericită.
back: I am not tired, I am happy.

en: He is not my brother, he is my colleague.
intent: Both clauses are about "he" (male, explicit): colegul meu. No setting changes anything.
ro: Nu e fratele mea, e colega mea.
back: He is not my brother, he is my colleague.
